minutes_text:
INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

A meeting of the Inglewood Arts Commission was convened on May 18, 2022, via Zoom. Commissioner Metcalf
called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. followed by the flag salute.
Roll Call
Present
  Commissioner Jacques Lesure, Commissioner at Large
  Commissioner Aletha Metcalf, District One
  Commissioner Onna Ehrlich-Bell, District Two
  Sabrina Barnes, Parks, Recreation, and Community Services Director
  Helen Lessick, Public Art Consultant
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  Commissioner Phyllis Battle, District Three
  Commissioner Vicki Perryman-Banks, District Four
Public Comments
  Holly Tempo, Board Member of Inglewood Open Studios (IOS) introduced herself and stated she is logging
in from Portugal and is honored to be here.
Approval of the Minutes
  Helen Lessick asked that the minutes from April 20, 2022 reflect the receipt of a letter from Susan Inglett
regarding Maren Hassinger’s project for Hollywood Park. Said letter was also read to the Commission by
Commissioner Metcalf following Mr. Witt’s quarterly report.
  Commissioner Lesure made the motion to approve the minutes from April 20, 2022. Commissioner Metcalf
seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Lesure, Ehrlich-Bell, and Metcalf
  Nays: None
Special Presentation
  Renée Fox, President of Inglewood Open Studios (IOS) introduced Board Members: Holly Tempo (Vice
President), Joyce Dallal (Secretary), Chris Mercier (Treasurer), and Minna Phillips (all present). Also mentioned were
Board Members Kali Nikitas and Adwin Brown (Advisor). She went on to give background on IOS, its
accomplishments to date, and contributions by the City of Inglewood. They are looking forward to working more
closely with the Arts Commission to expand opportunities for both Inglewood artists and residents using our
respective strengths.
  Commissioner Lesure stated it was great meeting Ms. Fox at the YOLA event and it’s also great that all
seven (7) board members have a strong connection to the Inglewood community. He asked Ms. Fox to share Board
Member’s connections to the city. Ms. Fox stated Wendy Chouteau is an Inglewood native, a former city employee
(Pool Manager), and owner of Custom Body Boot Camp located in the city. Holly Tempo has also lived and worked
  1
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

as an artist in the city. Chris Mercier is an architect and owns a firm in Inglewood on Hyde Park. Ms. Fox herself
moved from DC to Inglewood where it feels like home. Commissioner Lesure stated he's glad to hear the
connections. Ms. Fox also mentioned one of the IOS tours is what made Ms. Tempo move to the city. Commissioner
Metcalf asked if IOS was founded in 2006. Ms. Fox's stated yes. Commissioner Lesure asked if IOS uses the short or
long form for their 501 ©, are you able to raise a certain amount, and what is the cap on your yearly budget? Ms. Fox
stated IOS filed a short form and will start fundraising this year.
  Director Barnes stated the City has previously supported this event and asked if IOS plans to seek support
from the City for the 2022. Ms. Fox stated she does not have a formal request at the moment but is working with the
Board on a few items for a presentation at a future Arts Commission meeting or should she send the request to her.
Director Barnes asked that Ms. Fox send it to her in advance so it can be scheduled for a future Arts Commission
agenda and recommendation to the Mayor and Council.
  Commissioner Metcalf thanked Ms. Fox for her presentation and the IOS Board Members for joining the
meeting.

Verbal Reports
  Helen Lessick gave a verbal report regarding the following:
  •  IGAP 2022: Exploring Inglewood Trees RFQ which included information on artists’ city contracting
  requirements, the timeline, and the budget and how to apply plus outreach.
  •  Percent for Art Ordinance will celebrate its 20th anniversary in the summer of 2024. Staff proposes the City
  celebrate through production of an Inglewood Public Art Book ($25,000 - $30,000 estimated design and
  production expenses).
  •  Getty 25 Celebrated Inglewood on May 14 and 15, 2022 with co-host Beckman YOLA with music, food and
  fun. Tours of the Beckman YOLA Center were available as well as performances by YOLA musicians.
  Artisan booths were located throughout the City Hall south lawn and Grevillea Art Park.
Public Comments
  None
Commissioner’s Comments
  None
With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 7:24 p.m.
